description: The Global Iron Ore Mines Tracker (GIOMT) from Global Energy Monitor provides asset-level information on iron ore mines worldwide, including operating, proposed, shelved, retired and mothballed mines. It was built to show the geographic concentration of iron ore capacity that shapes downstream iron and steel production and the transition to low-carbon steel. On 26 September 2026 the page counted 949 mines in 74 countries and areas, more than 250 owners and 4.8 billion tonnes of annual capacity, dominated by Australia, Brazil and China. Each mine has ownership, development and operating status, design capacity, annual production since 2022, and reserves and resources; some mines are reported together as a complex when finer data are lacking. The first release was November 2024, with a limited update for new and retired assets in August 2025. Access is a free tracker map, summary tables and a spreadsheet download after a request form, under CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: grouped complexes hide individual pits, and production is reported only where companies disclose it. For simulation it supports supply-chain disruption and hazard exposure studies of steelmaking inputs. Related catalogue records include the Global Coal Mine Tracker and the global mining polygons of Maus et al.
